newsitem.title: USA: Quality Dining wants bagel divestiture by 90 days.
newsitem.headline: Quality Dining wants bagel divestiture by 90 days.

text.p: Quality Dining Inc, a restaurant company, said Monday it hopes to divest its bagel-related business within 60 to 90 days.

"We continue to work actively on the divestiture of our bagel-related businesses and are in discussions with several interested parties," chief executive officer Daniel Fitzpatrick said in a news release.
The company said in May it planned to divest its Bruegger's Bagel Bakeries-related businesses.

The company Monday reported a net loss of $201.7 million or $11.93 a share for the second quarter ended May 11, compared to net income of $2.1 million or $0.24 a share a year ago, due largely to a non-cash impairment charge of $185.0 million associated with the divestiture.

General and administrative expenses increased significantly in the second quarter to $9.7 million resulting from the development of a regional and corporate infrastructure designed to support the terminated Franchise Operating Partner Program and what had been an anticipated as aggressive development of the Bruegger's Bagel Bakery concept, the company said.

Earnings performance was hurt by lower than expected profits from company-owned Bruegger's Bagel Bakeries and Grady's American Grill restaurants, lower than expected franchise revenues and higher than expected interest expense, the company said.

"We will continue to aggressively operate all of our businesses with a focus on improving sales and margin performance," Fitzpatrick said. "At the corporate level, we have initiated programs to realign our resources to ensure efficient and cost-effective support for our restaurant operations. This realignment should reduce our general and administrative expenses significantly."
Quality Dining shares were down 1/2 at 5-1/4 Monday.
